name: The Drawbridge

pitch_detail.notes: Easy fifth-class climbing to escape the rockfall line.
Crux pitch: mid-5.10-ish face climbing with a short aid section.
Traverse out of a dihedral on a tricky flake; surmount a roof on the left via cracks and stemming; extensive cleaning of dirt/moss-covered slabs.
Route gains the ridge proper; rock quality improves and climbing becomes more moderate aside from one short, harder hand-and-fist crack.
Final technical pitch, delicately around teetering blocks, before moderate snow slopes lead ~400 ft to the summit.

descent_text: Descend the south side of the peak and the East Ridge back toward camp; the first-ascent party described this walk-off as straightforward ('breezy'), regaining camp near twilight.
approach: The lawful approach is from the US side: cross Ross Lake by boat, follow the Lightning Creek trail and the abandoned Freezeout Creek trail, then work round to the glacier below the north face. The first-ascent party instead came in from Canada — from Lightning Lake in Manning Provincial Park, BC, up and over Frosty Mountain, into Princess Creek basin, across the Princess/Crow Creek divide and down into the Crow Creek drainage — but walking into the US away from a port of entry is not a lawful crossing. On that line the first-ascent party camped on the only dry spot on the ridge, about two-thirds of the way down to the approach glacier.
overview: A 2017 first ascent up the previously unclimbed central buttress of Castle Peak's north face, directly below the summit — sustained 5.10+ face and crack climbing with one short aid section on the crux pitch, finishing on moderate snow slopes about 400 ft below the top.
beta: Despite the north face already hosting several routes since its 1979 first ascent, the central buttress directly below the summit remained untouched until Morgan Zentler and Jason Schilling's 2017 ascent. They started with easy 5th-class climbing to escape the rockfall line, then hit a crux pitch (pitch 2) of mid-5.10/5.11-ish face climbing requiring a short aid move. Subsequent pitches traverse out of a dihedral on a tricky flake and surmount a roof on the left via fun but hard cracks and stemming; the middle section demanded extensive cleaning of dirt- and moss-covered slabs. After about five pitches the route gains the ridge proper, where the rock quality improves and climbing becomes more moderate, aside from one short, harder hand-and-fist crack. The final technical pitch dances delicately around teetering blocks before moderate snow slopes lead the last 400 ft to the summit.
gear: Ice axe/crampons for approach glacier and summit snow slopes
fa: Morgan Zentler and Jason Schilling, June 2017
face: North Face, central buttress (directly below the summit)
